newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran police seize 410 kg of opium in armed clashes.
newsitem.headline: Iran police seize 410 kg of opium in armed clashes.

text.p: Iranian police confiscated 410 kg (900 lb) of opium after armed clashes with drug traffickers in the north-eastern province of Khorasan, the official Iranian news agency IRNA said on Sunday.
"During the clashes 14 traffickers were arrested and handed over to the provincial Islamic revolutionary court," IRNA said, quoting a report released on Saturday.
It did not say when the clashes took place.
Iran is a key transit route for drugs being smuggled from Afghanistan and Pakistan through Turkey to Europe.

According to Iranian law, possession of five kg (11 lb) of opium or 30 grams (just over one ounce) of heroin is punishable by death. More than 1,000 people have been executed in drug-related cases since the law took effect in 1989.
